A weekly worked example

Source: vignettes/a04_example.Rmd
a04_example.Rmd

This example uses synthetic intervals to build weekly trajectories with four states: alive with or without recorded pneumonia history, and death with or without that history. The analyst defines these states; the two death states describe prior history, not cause of death. Each target interval ends at death or the end of observation.

Five patient histories

All patients enter on January 1, 2020. The examples cover:

  • 001: three weeks without pneumonia.
  • 002: pneumonia recorded on January 9, with history retained to observation end.
  • 003: pneumonia on January 10 and death on January 12, in the same weekly cycle.
  • 004: death without pneumonia history on January 4.
  • 005: observation ending on January 10, partway through the second cycle.
states <- c(
  "Alive, no recorded pneumonia",
  "Alive, pneumonia history",
  "Death, no pneumonia history",
  "Death, pneumonia history"
)

interval <- function(id, state, start, end) {
  data.frame(
    subject_id = id,
    cohort_definition_id = state,
    cohort_start_date = as.Date(start),
    cohort_end_date = as.Date(end)
  )
}

input <- do.call(rbind, list(
  interval("001", "0", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-21"),
  interval("001", states[1], "2020-01-01", "2020-01-21"),
  interval("002", "0", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-21"),
  interval("002", states[1], "2020-01-01", "2020-01-08"),
  interval("002", states[2], "2020-01-09", "2020-01-15"),
  interval("002", states[2], "2020-01-12", "2020-01-21"),
  interval("003", "0", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-12"),
  interval("003", states[1], "2020-01-01", "2020-01-09"),
  interval("003", states[2], "2020-01-10", "2020-01-11"),
  interval("003", states[4], "2020-01-12", "2020-01-12"),
  interval("004", "0", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-04"),
  interval("004", states[1], "2020-01-01", "2020-01-03"),
  interval("004", states[3], "2020-01-04", "2020-01-04"),
  interval("005", "0", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-10"),
  interval("005", states[1], "2020-01-01", "2020-01-10")
))

Import combines 002’s overlapping history records without counting shared days twice.

Choose the weekly rules

Death takes priority over either living state. Pneumonia history takes priority over the state without pneumonia. Both death states are absorbing, so no further cycles are generated after a selected death cycle.

studyPath <- tempfile("c2t-weekly-example-")
dir.create(studyPath)

allowed <- stats::setNames(list(
  states,
  states[c(2, 4)],
  character(0),
  character(0)
), states)

study <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "WeeklyExample",
  pathToStudy = studyPath,
  useCDM = FALSE,
  trajectoryDataObject = input,
  stateCohortLabels = states,
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = states[c(4, 3, 2, 1)],
  stateCohortAbsorbing = states[c(3, 4)],
  allowedStatesList = allowed,
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  cycleLength = 7
)
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = study)
trajectories <- createTrajectories(studyEnv = study)

Inspect the weekly histories 

clinical <- subset(trajectories, !state_label %in% c("START", "EXIT"))
knitr::kable(clinical[c(
  "subject_id", "state_label", "state_start_date", "state_end_date"
)], row.names = FALSE)
subject_id state_label state_start_date state_end_date
001 Alive, no recorded pneumonia 2020-01-01 2020-01-07
001 Alive, no recorded pneumonia 2020-01-08 2020-01-14
001 Alive, no recorded pneumonia 2020-01-15 2020-01-21
002 Alive, no recorded pneumonia 2020-01-01 2020-01-07
002 Alive, pneumonia history 2020-01-08 2020-01-14
002 Alive, pneumonia history 2020-01-15 2020-01-21
003 Alive, no recorded pneumonia 2020-01-01 2020-01-07
003 Death, pneumonia history 2020-01-08 2020-01-12
004 Death, no pneumonia history 2020-01-01 2020-01-04
005 Alive, no recorded pneumonia 2020-01-01 2020-01-07
005 Alive, no recorded pneumonia 2020-01-08 2020-01-10

For 003, cycle two is labelled Death, pneumonia history. It preserves the history category but not the January 10 onset date as a separate row.

For 004, the first cycle is a death cycle even though death occurred on January 4. Row dates describe the cycle. Both patients’ final cycles end on their death dates because their target intervals end there. With a later target endpoint, absorption would stop after the cycle without shortening it to the event date.

For 005, the second cycle covers January 8 to 10. Its January 11 EXIT marker adds no observed time and does not indicate death.

The completed run saves these rules in WeeklyExample/Settings/analysisSettings.rds. See Import cohort data to rerun them with fresh data in a new location.

Before fitting a model

The four labels can be four model states. For a model of onset followed by mortality within a week, create a second view retaining pneumonia history instead of selecting death. Keep identical patient-week boundaries and observation endpoints in both views, with no weeks added after death. TMA’s prepareStageObservations() pairs them and estimateStageTransitions() fits the stages. See TMA’s inst/examples/c2t-to-icer.R for an intervention example.

A requirement that pneumonia precede death by at least one day belongs in the cohort definitions. Weekly labels cannot establish that separation. Use the underlying intervals when exact dates matter; Read the output lists their locations.
